brief.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix rally +5-8% on US chip rebound; foreign buying continues, but memory pair trade diverges as HBM capacity tensions persist
brief.summary: <cite index="23-6,23-7,23-8">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rallied sharply on July 22, with Samsung up 5.6% and SK Hynix up 8.4%, following overnight semiconductor strength on Wall Street.</cite> <cite index="26-3,26-4">Foreign investors net bought $908.5M of SK Hynix and $424M of Samsung on July 22 alone, with three-day totals reaching $1.13B in Samsung and $1.07B in SK Hynix.</cite> <cite index="25-1,25-14,25-16">However, top 1% domestic traders at Mirae Asset Securities net-bought Samsung while net-selling SK Hynix as profit-taking continues.</cite> <cite index="11-1,15-1,15-2">DRAM contract prices are projected to rise 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026, with NAND up 10-15%, as HBM capacity allocation continues to squeeze mainstream memory supply.</cite> <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix held 57% global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025 versus Samsung's 22% and Micron's 21%.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Favor SK Hynix over Samsung on HBM leadership; foreign flow supports both but smart money rotating out of Hynix into Samsung post-rally. <cite index="5-3">SK Hynix expected to maintain ~50% HBM market share in 2026.</cite> <cite index="5-4">Near-term noise around Nvidia negotiations with all three suppliers and Samsung's HBM3E qualification progress creates tactical volatility.</cite> <cite index="25-8">Samsung buying interpreted as bargain hunting after recent correction amid AI chip peak concerns.</cite> <cite index="26-6">SK Hynix fell 39.6% from June 22 high to July 20 low, creating valuation dislocation.</cite> Relative call: neutral to slight Samsung overweight on catch-up trade, but Hynix retains structural HBM edge.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="16-9,16-10">Q1 2026 saw extraordinary 93-98% QoQ DRAM contract price increases; Q2-Q3 2026 showing deceleration but still double-digit gains.</cite> <cite index="11-9,11-10">AI demand keeps DRAM/NAND supply constrained while manufacturers shift capacity to higher-margin server products, leaving less for consumer memory.</cite> <cite index="12-10,12-11">Prices expected to increase up to 50% in Q3 2026 with another 40% in Q4; shortages forecast through 2028 if AI consumption continues.</cite> <cite index="6-11,6-12">Risk of production increases over next three years easing supply constraints if AI demand grows at normal pace; current share prices assume high prices and discipline persist.</cite>

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="8-4,8-12">Top three memory makers have allocated full HBM output for 2026; Micron guided 68% gross margin in Q2 2026.</cite> <cite index="5-1,5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B gigabits; TSMC's AI demand running ahead of forecasts.</cite> <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only minimal to modest HBM3E price downtick for 2026 vs 2025 as more suppliers come online.</cite> <cite index="1-5">Micron announced integration of HBM3E 36GB 12-high into AMD Instinct MI350 Series.</cite> <cite index="8-3">HBM3E consumes roughly 3x the wafer area of standard DRAM.</cite> Structural supply tightness persists through 2027.
